summary: Independent Stage 1 security review found four reproducible blockers in structural output handling: credentials in JSON property names bypass the floor, duplicate serialized JSON members can reintroduce credentials after parsed-value validation, local $ref siblings are ignored, and browser-decoded/srcset image URLs bypass auto-fetch detection. Existing focused suites passed 78/78 but did not cover these boundary evasions. Attacker-controlled schema keys and refs do not leak into reasons; optional undefined values correctly fail closed per the approved T19 contract. Stage 2 stopped after Stage 1 failed. Scanner behavior concurrently edited in service/types/schemas was excluded. No global quality PASS is claimed.
summary_markdown: T24 structural-output review: **Stage 1 FAIL** with four blockers. Exact offline reproductions and immutable logs are recorded in `T24-review.md` and `T24-stage1-probe.ts`; Stage 2 was stopped as required.

changed_files.change: created exact offline public-boundary reproductions and clean controls

artifacts.summary: Independent two-skill Stage 1 review with four blocker findings, exact attack vectors, fixes, class-scope enumeration, clean controls, immutable evidence, and routing audit.
Offline synthetic probe for property-name disclosure, duplicate-key persistence, $ref sibling validation, reason safety, undefined handling, encoded/srcset exfiltration, and a public-link control.

acceptance.criterion: Tool/resource/error/SDK output contains no synthetic secret and carries safe sibling metadata without altering operation JSON.
acceptance.evidence: F-001 reproduces a recognized credential in an enumerable JSON property name crossing dispatchCallTool with isError false and redaction state none. Ordinary error messages and sibling metadata remained leak-safe and the real SDK round-trip passed.

acceptance.criterion: Safe numeric values and IDs are retained; recognized secrets cannot bypass by field key; unsafe numeric/schema cases return format-unsafe.
acceptance.evidence: Existing numeric and ID controls pass, attacker schema keys and refs do not leak into reason tokens, and undefined fails closed per T19. F-001 bypasses by property key, while F-003 accepts a value violating a supported sibling constraint next to local $ref.

acceptance.criterion: Disabled advisory settings cannot disable the deterministic floor; persistence applies it; public links remain allowed while auto-fetch exfiltration is blocked.
acceptance.evidence: Ordinary disabled-floor and persistence fixtures pass and the public-link control is unchanged. F-002 leaks a credential through duplicate serialized members into persistence; F-004 leaves entity-encoded src and srcset auto-fetch URLs unchanged.

acceptance.criterion: Review remains independent, bounded, schema-valid, and excludes concurrently changing recursive scanner behavior.
acceptance.evidence: No source, git, flow, package, dependency, model, or network action was taken. Scanner behavior was excluded after service.ts changed during review. Evidence is confined to focused existing tests and synthetic offline probes.

findings.problem: The structural JSON walker scans property values but copies property names verbatim, so a recognized credential used as an enumerable key reaches MCP output with redaction.state none.
findings.impact: An untrusted tool or resource can disclose a credential to the MCP client in operation JSON while the sibling metadata falsely reports no redaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Inspect own enumerable string property descriptors and return format-unsafe when a property name contains a redactable secret or PII span; add direct validator and MCP transport regressions.
findings.evidence: The offline T24 probe showed property-name leakage through both the core validator and MCP transport while MCP returned a non-error result.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Complete validator read plus ctx searches for Object.entries, Object.fromEntries, and validateToolOutput enumerated the only object reconstruction path and its public MCP adapter.

findings.problem: The adapter validates JSON.parse(content), then restores the original bytes when the parsed value has no findings; duplicate members can hide a recognized secret in an overwritten value.
findings.impact: A generated serialized JSON payload can persist or return a recognized credential through the mandatory floor, including when advisory security is disabled.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the original serialized text to pass the deterministic text floor before byte-identical return, and add a duplicate-member persistence regression; apply the same rule to the exported MCP compatibility wrapper.
findings.evidence: The offline T24 probe logged duplicateKeySerialized.leaked=true and duplicateKeyPersistence.allowed=true/leaked=true in .metaproject/data/gdctx/raw/2026-09-06T12-47-01-651Z_run.log.

class_scope.enumeration_method: ctx searches for JSON.parse(content), byte-preserving no-redaction returns, and every validateSerializedOutput call enumerated both wrappers and all current consumers.

findings.problem: The output schema screen accepts a local $ref with supported validation siblings, but the underlying validator returns immediately after the reference and ignores those siblings.
findings.impact: A tool value that violates its declared operation schema is transmitted with isError false, silently corrupting the client's output contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate supported siblings after the referenced schema, or reject $ref plus validation siblings as unsupported until the validator implements them; add core and MCP regressions.
findings.evidence: The offline T24 probe used a local string $ref with minLength 20 and value short; the core returned ok=true and MCP returned refSiblingIsError=false in .metaproject/data/gdctx/raw/2026-09-06T12-47-01-651Z_run.log.

class_scope.enumeration_method: ctx search for schema.$ref, $ref.startsWith, and resolveRef across the output screen and underlying validator enumerated every reference handling site.

findings.problem: Auto-fetch detection classifies only raw http(s)/protocol-relative strings and only HTML src, so browser-decoded src values and srcset candidates are released unchanged.
findings.impact: Rendering attacker-controlled tool/resource/error text can make a zero-click request to an attacker host and disclose attacker-encoded context.
findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalize HTML character references for URL classification while preserving source offsets, enumerate srcset candidates, and add entity/srcset/Markdown entity regressions while retaining the public-link control.
findings.evidence: The offline T24 probe logged encodedHtmlImageChanged=false and srcsetHtmlImageChanged=false; ordinaryLinkChanged also remained false in .metaproject/data/gdctx/raw/2026-09-06T12-47-01-651Z_run.log.

class_scope.enumeration_method: ctx search for exfilHost, INLINE, REFERENCE_DEF, HTML_IMG, and srcset enumerated every auto-fetch parser; no srcset implementation exists.
